extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD implementers and managers of the Commercial Activities (CA) program — OPNAV-443 staff, major/sub-claimants, contracting officers, contract administration staffs, QAEs, COTRs
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and evaluative criteria for executing the Navy's Commercial Activities (CA) program, including how to prepare Performance Work Statements, estimate and monitor costs, staff and train contract administration, and manage post-award/contingency issues for contracted base support functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized claimant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for centralized guidance at the claimant level throughout the CA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff CA Program implementation offices with enough personnel (at least two people) to oversee transitions; create field CA implementation teams to conduct on-site assistance at milestones (PWS writing, MEO formation, cost comparison); publish periodic 'Lessons Learned' synopses and submit recaps to OPNAV-443; convene command transition meetings 60–90 days prior to contractor transition to solicit leadership support and surface problem areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide systematic direction on post-award issues (currently instructions focus on pre-award only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPNAV-443 should issue an instruction on converting to contractor operations outlining options for dealing with contractor performance problems, contingency planning, streamlined personnel recruiting/detailing, streamlined procedures for bringing onboard temporary contractors, and guidance on contract administration and performance problem resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance (QA) manuals and sampling guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants should publish a Quality Assurance Manual to assist transitioned commands in establishing QA programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual should include policy on sampling techniques, sample checklists, measurement issues, and be a practical 'how to' for QAEs; claimants should establish QAE training or obtain quotas from other claimancies offering such courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and clarity of the Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: PWSs must precisely define all necessary task requirements to reduce delays, avoid increased costs, and produce accurate savings estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex operations (e.g., storage/warehousing, multi-function contracts) require greater resources and expertise to write adequate PWSs; invest resources in PWS preparation, consider funding additional resources during cost comparison for PWS formulation, develop CA functional experts at claimant level to assist in PWS preparation, and audit complex-operation PWS adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource allocation for PWS preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate sufficient resources during cost comparison to develop an adequate PWS, particularly for complex operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most commands do not allocate sufficient resources 'out of hide' and produce poorly written or incomplete PWSs; consider financially assisting commands during initial stages so adequate resources are devoted to defining performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of negotiated procurement for complex operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiated procurement (two-step) should be the only type of procurement allowed for complex operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed-bid (one-step) procurements appear to impact quality of performance negatively in complex operations; negotiated procurement allows more flexibility in defining requirements and selecting qualified contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type choice and incentives (Cost Plus Award Fee vs Firm Fixed Price)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider contract types that streamline QA requirements and provide positive incentives to contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents preferred Cost Plus Award Fee over Firm Fixed Price because award fee is not subject to the Disputes Clause and has less documentation burden when performance cannot be assured. Conduct cost analyses comparing contract administration costs and performance quality under both contract types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for multifunction (BOS) contracts where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine small single-function contracts into larger multifunction/Base Operating Support (BOS) contracts to improve flexibility and economies of scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multifunction contracts provide a single point of contractor contact, more-qualified management structure, ability to hire experienced staff, and simplify government contract administration via a single Service Contract Manager (SCM); consider as option where activities include several functions in CA inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration staffing adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure contract administration staffing is sufficient to provide quality surveillance and QA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost Comparison Handbook staffing estimates (4–6% or OMB staffing standards) often underestimate actual needs, especially for large or complex contracts; inadequate staffing or collateral-duty administration leads to diminished surveillance; claimants should be willing to negotiate QA staffing and possibly exceed handbook/OMB minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate estimation and monitoring of contract administration costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must accurately reflect post-award contract administration costs, which routinely exceed initial estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual administration costs frequently exceed the typical 4–8% range used in estimates; implement closer monitoring through improved cost control/accounting systems and develop better cost yardsticks for evaluating CAs after decisions are made; Chapter V recommends control systems to monitor contract admin and other post-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved cost accounting systems and cost yardsticks
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial/accounting systems must capture costs by CA function to allow meaningful comparisons of estimated vs actual costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing systems do not capture costs by function, making development/comparison of estimates arduous; managers should plan better methods for determining cost effectiveness and OPNAV should develop cost yardsticks and better accounting for post-award costs (contract administration, litigation, contingency costs, clerical support, training, morale, loss of budget flexibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize use of standard cost factors (e.g., fringe benefits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard cost factor for government retirement/fringe benefits (27.05% used in CA cost comparisons) should be reviewed for accuracy and consistency with other labor acceleration factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancy between 27.05% and 16–17% used elsewhere raises questions; use of averages can distort estimates when costs vary widely across functions; research the rationale and reconcile differences or adjust assumptions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and account for 'hidden' or unrecorded costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and include unrecorded/underestimated costs of contracting out (contract admin, contingency/performance costs, litigation, clerical support, training, morale, loss of budget flexibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These costs frequently translate into loss of managerial flexibility, morale decline, and degraded performance; identifying and reducing these costs can involve: centralized guidance, better PWSs, well-implemented QA programs, post-award guidance, and better training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish contingency planning and a central contingency fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide guidance and financial assistance to assemble contingency operations when contractors perform poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend OPNAV-443 establish a central contingency fund to help activities rid themselves of deficient contractors until resolicitation; streamline procedures for assembling temporary government or contractor operations; delineate contingency plan options in post-award instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilization readiness and contract clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure contractors are prepared to perform under mobilization/emergency conditions and that solicitation/contracts delineate mobilization requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LMI recommended installation managers: have mobilization plans, delineate mobilization requirements in solicitations, include mobilization clauses, require contractors to plan for recall of former military to active duty, and include contractors in mobilization planning and exercises where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contractors in installation mobilization planning and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, incorporate primary contractors into mobilization planning and exercises to ensure readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation helps validate contractor readiness; most contracts for low-skill services can be expanded in mobilization, but critical administrative/logistics/engineering contracts should take steps to ensure readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for CA implementation staff and related roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand and improve training on CA program for implementation staffs, KOs, COTRs, QAEs, and claimancy personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should be more comprehensive, better publicized and accessible; address cost comparison process, PWS formulation, contract administration options, and contractual methods; avoid using instructors without real CA experience; increase course quotas or provide additional courses to meet demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized KO training and KO involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Contracting Officers (KOs) are trained in CA implementation and contractual options to guide selection of procurement/contract vehicle and evaluation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KO normally leads in choosing procurement type and contract vehicle; gaps in KO knowledge warrant additional research and specialized training to ensure best-value decisions for conversions to contract operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field assistance and milestone visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide on-site assistance to activities at key milestones to transfer lessons learned and build practical expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field visits should coincide with PWS writing, MEO formation, cost comparison, and other milestones so activities benefit from experiences of others and claimant-level expertise is grounded in 'real-life' practice rather than only instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and solicit 'lessons learned'
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a periodic synopsis of CA program lessons learned and solicit inputs from transitioned activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute lessons widely, use them to improve claimant guidance, and submit recaps annually to OPNAV-443 to propagate best practices and avoid repeat mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider excluding complex operations from CA inventory or assist financially
rubrics_metrics.description: If complex operations consistently yield inadequately defined PWSs and high hidden costs, evaluate whether to remove them from CA inventory or provide financial assistance to prepare PWSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct audits/research on complex/multi-function contracts to determine PWS adequacy; based on findings, either eliminate some complex operations from CA inventory or fund additional resources during cost comparison to ensure adequate PWS formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess tradeoffs between automation investment and contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare investment in automation/technology vs CA program for complex operations to determine best return on investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some complex operations, investment in automation, improved computer tech, and robotics may yield better ROI than contracting out; consider reallocating resources from PWS/C A prep to efficiency/automation programs if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closer monitoring of post-award events to substantiate program outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement formal post-award control systems to collect accurate cost and performance data so program success/failure can be objectively assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current monitoring is loosely structured; proponents rely on pre-award estimates, opponents on anecdotal evidence; without systematic post-award accounting, claims about CA program savings are suspect; establish control systems as recommended in Chapter V.
